tool_summary: Modifies an existing user account's properties, including group membership, shell, and lock status.
platform_notes: usermod is a GNU/Linux (shadow-utils) tool; macOS has no direct equivalent (dscl is used instead). This ruleset targets Linux only.

rules.description: The -o/--non-unique flag combined with a -u/--uid value of 0 changes an account's UID to 0, granting it full root privileges while keeping its original username.
rules.notes: Same privilege escalation pattern as useradd -o -u 0, applied to an existing account.

rules.description: The -aG/-G flags add the target user to supplementary groups. Adding a user to a privileged group such as sudo, wheel, or docker grants that user root-equivalent access without changing their UID.
rules.reversible_note: Group membership can be reverted, but any access exercised under the elevated group in the meantime is not undone.
rules.notes: args_any list covers common privileged group names; not exhaustive. Host-specific privileged groups are not detectable by commandant.

rules.description: The -L/--lock flag disables the account's password, and -e/--expiredate in the past forces immediate expiration. Both can deny account access.
rules.reversible_note: Reversible with -U/--unlock unless the account's own owner was relying on access in the interim.

rules.description: Modifies an existing user account's properties. Depending on the flags used, this can change shell, home directory, or other account attributes with downstream effects on access.
rules.reversible_note: Most attributes can be changed back, but the specific effect depends entirely on which attribute is modified.
